en: Preface to the Collected Annotations on the *Tiantai Sijiao Yi* The *Tiantai Sijiao Yi* is truly the essential path of the Exoteric Teachings (*shijiao*). From antiquity to the present, there have been many commentators; however, some were too brief and incomplete, while others were so expansive as to be overly prolix. Furthermore, they often excised the original text, merely marking the beginning and end.

Unless one is thoroughly versed in recitation, it is difficult to peruse them. Now, I have collected the texts from various sections and annotated them beneath the main text. Will this not facilitate reading and study? As for the occasional discrepancies between my views and those of other masters, these simply record what I heard from my predecessors.

Virtue does not consist in following one's own arbitrary whims. As for the methods of contemplation in the initial vehicle (*ādikarmika-yāna*)—which rectify the end of literary expression though the texts are concise, their principles are nonetheless complete. If those who are new to study apply their minds to this, forgetting words and forgetting thought, casting away both the trap and the fish-catcher, how could it be otherwise?
If one can achieve such a state, there is nothing that cannot be realized; yet how could this be apart from these very teachings?
Preface respectfully composed by the śramaṇa Mōngrùn of South India, on the fifth day of the fifth month of the summer in the year of Yuánsōng Jiǎxū (1334).
